contract.label: Toggle
contract.summary: A two-state button that holds a pressed/on state — the control for a horizon or overlay switch ("Previous week", "Compare"), never a Button swapping variants to fake one.

parts.name: Toggle
parts.description: Pressable button toggling a pressed/on state. The outline variant casts no shadow, so it sits level with the outline buttons and connected groups beside it in a toolbar.

props.name: surface
props.description: What the toggle sits on — default inside a card, sheet, dialog or table row, where an outline toggle rests clear so the surface shows through; page straight on the shell's muted content area, where it rests and hovers like an outline Button so a toolbar reads as one surface. Only the outline variant has a face to swap; the ghost default needs nothing on either.

rules: **A two-state switch is an outline `Toggle`.** A horizon or overlay switch — "Previous week", "Compare to last period" — is a `Toggle` with `variant="outline"` that holds its pressed state, never a `Button` swapping `variant` to fake one. It casts no shadow, so it sits level with the outline buttons and connected groups beside it.

**`layout` is a `toggle-group`'s shape.** `connected` joins the items into one strip with no frame — the range presets or interval switcher in a chart header or toolbar, the same height as the controls beside it — and is the default for an outline group. `spaced` sets ghost items a gap apart inside a padded, bordered frame — a formatting toolbar, where the frame is what groups them — and is the default for a ghost group. Cite it as a variant axis; `spacing={0}` is its alias in code.

**Pick the surface by what is underneath.** An outline toggle placed straight on the shell's `muted` content area — a toolbar, a filter row — takes `surface="page"`, which rests and hovers like an outline Button (`outline-surface`, `outline-hover`), so the row reads as one surface. Inside a `card`, `sheet`, `dialog` or table row it keeps `default`. The ghost `default` variant has no resting face on either, exactly like a ghost Button, so `surface` leaves it alone.

A `toggle-group` placed straight on the shell's `muted` content area — an interval or view switcher in a toolbar — takes `surface="page"`, so it rests and hovers like the outline Buttons beside it. A connected group puts the face on its outline items; a spaced group puts it on its frame and the items inside stay `default`. Inside a `card`, `sheet`, `dialog` or table row it keeps `default`.
examples: `<Toggle variant="outline">Previous week</Toggle>` beside `<ToggleGroup variant="outline" layout="connected">` in a chart header, every control at `size="default"`.
`<Toggle variant="outline" surface="page" aria-label="Compare to last period">Compare</Toggle>` beside `<Button variant="outline">` in a toolbar on the page body.
`<ToggleGroup variant="outline" layout="connected" surface="page" defaultValue={["hourly"]}>` in a filter row on the page body.
antiPatterns: A `Button` whose `variant` flips between `default` and `outline` to show that an overlay is on — that is a `Toggle`, which carries the pressed state for assistive tech and the design alike.
An outline group drawn as a spaced frame beside a toggle, standing taller than the controls on its row — the presets are `layout="connected"`.

An outline toggle on the muted page body given `bg-background`, `bg-card` or `bg-white` instead of `surface="page"` — in dark mode `background` is darker than `card`, so the toggle sinks below the cards beside it.

A toggle group on the muted page body given `bg-background`, `bg-card` or `bg-white` instead of `surface="page"` — in dark mode `background` is darker than `card`, so the group sinks below the cards beside it.
